content.text: The Mistake Almost Every Creator Makes First

The mistake is thinking that platforms like Stripe or PayPal are the only game in town. They're not. In fact, these platforms have made a conscious decision to restrict access to creators in certain countries, leaving them with limited payment options and high fees. But creators can work around this by building their own digital commerce infrastructure, using tools like Cloudflare Pages, Cloudflare Workers, and NOWPayments. This approach may seem daunting at first, but it's actually a more secure and cost-effective way to sell digital products internationally.
Why This Keeps Happening Even to Experienced Sellers

This problem persists because creators often don't understand the importance of infrastructure sovereignty. They think that as long as they're selling their products, they're doing everything right. But the truth is, infrastructure has nothing to do with sales; it's about control. When creators build their businesses on platforms that can take down their infrastructure at any moment, they're putting their businesses at risk. Experienced sellers fall into this trap because they're often too proud to admit they don't know better.
The Real Cost of Getting This Wrong

The real cost of getting this wrong is high. Creators who rely on platforms like Stripe or PayPal for international transactions are subject to high fees, currency conversion rates, and even outright account closures. But it's not just the financial costs that are a problem; it's the loss of control and autonomy that comes with building your business on someone else's infrastructure. When the platform changes its rules, creators are left scrambling to adapt, losing valuable time and money in the process.
